findings.body: The convention explicitly permits Agentation's lazy chunk in the built assets. The scaffold Dockerfile builds the frontend once without `APP_ENV` (`src/forge/templates/skeleton/Dockerfile:6`), so the production build can contain the toolbar code even though the runtime check prevents it from loading. The Done-when item requires Agentation to be absent from production builds. Specify separate demo and production builds with the toolbar excluded from the latter.
findings.title: Not done: Anyone can point at the screen

findings.body: The example counts tables before opening the insertion transaction. During a rolling deployment, the previous instance can create the first real row after the counts but before the demo records are inserted (`src/forge/templates/conventions/deploy.md:5-6`). The loader would then mix demo and real data despite the stated refusal rule. The check and insertion need a database guard that makes a concurrent first write cause refusal or retry.
findings.title: Make the empty-table check atomic with demo insertion

findings.body: The stack convention tells builders to add the loader, but the unchanged Forge skill's prototype instructions at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:103-111` do not tell the agent to build it in the first version or use `Words they use` for screen labels. The story assigns the skill edit to SPEC, outside this part's scope.
findings.title: Later: SPEC must put first-version demo data and customer labels in the skill

findings.body: The frontend convention describes clicking an element and pasting feedback, but the unchanged Forge skill at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:103-111` gives salespeople no Agentation instructions. The story assigns that skill edit to DEMO, outside this part's scope.
findings.title: Later: DEMO must put the pointing instructions in the skill
